Seminar Title:

Development of an Adversary-aware Robust Gait Recognition Framework for Secure Video Surveillance System

Seminar Type:

Registration Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Speaker Name:

Rittick Maity ( Rollno : 523ec2012)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

ECE Seminar Hall (EC-303)

Date and Time:

06 Oct 2026 12:10 pm

Contact:

Manish Okade

Abstract:

Human gait is the manner of walking and a biometric trait that can be acquired passively,&nbspremotely, and without the subject&rsquos cooperation. First, accuracy on unconstrained benchmarks&nbspremains limited, while leading results rely on multi-GPU training and large batches. Second, adversarial&nbsprobustness has received limited study, mainly on the 124-subject CASIA-B dataset, with&nbspno large-scale defence evaluation on wild benchmarks. Third, end-to-end embedded deployment&nbspremains unaddressed. A compact silhouette-based network, CoordGait, is therefore proposed. It&nbspplaces a three-dimensional coordinate attention block and a grouped seven-frame temporal branch&nbspwithin a pseudo-three-dimensional residual trunk whose stage transitions use Haar wavelet downsampling.&nbspUnder a unified single-GPU protocol, CoordGait achieves 64.39% Rank-1 accuracy on&nbspGait3D with about 11 million parameters, outperforming DeepGaitV2 by 2.5 points and TrackletGait&nbspby 1.7 points under the same budget, while achieving 63.70% Rank-1 on GREW. The&nbspadversarial vulnerability of four modern recognisers is evaluated on Gait3D, where an imperceptible&nbspperturbation with ϵ = 0.05 reduces clean accuracy by 60.7&ndash89.5%. A DDPM-based purification&nbspdefence, trained only on clean silhouettes, restores attacked Rank-1 from 14.3% to 61.4%, recovering&nbsp94% of the lost accuracy with only a 0.5-point drop on clean inputs and no recogniser retraining.&nbspIt holds under a fully adaptive attacker using backward pass differentiable approximation together&nbspwith expectation over transformation, and it generalises across four recognisers and across datasets.&nbspPurification depends on one free parameter, the noise level, and the wrong choice of that parameter&nbspcosts up to 21.5 Rank-1 points. A self-consistency criterion purifies each input twice with independent&nbspnoise and compares the resulting embeddings to identify failed purification without training,&nbsplabels, or estimates of attack strength. It achieves an AUC of 0.9991, transfers across three recognition&nbsparchitectures, and resists explicit evasion attempts.
